deities: Gayatri (second wife of Brahma; both idols installed here, Savitri worshipped first)

history.period: Temple built 1687 per some sources, but others say the early 20th century by the Bangar family; the Savitri idol is claimed to date to the 7th century AD (conflicting; verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the Savitri Temple is not in Ajmer town - it stands atop Ratnagiri Hill at Pushkar, district Ajmer, Rajasthan (~15 km northwest of Ajmer). Dedicated to Goddess Savitri, Brahma's first wife: legend says that when Brahma performed his yajna at Pushkar without Savitri (marrying Gayatri to complete the rites), the enraged Savitri cursed Brahma and retreated to Ratnagiri Hill, where she merged with the hill and emerged as the Savitri Jharna spring that flows beside the temple. By agreement Savitri is always worshipped first, then Gayatri - a tradition continuing today, with both idols installed in the shrine. The construction date is conflicted: Rajasthan Tour Planner gives 1687, while Pushkar guides say the Bangar family built it in the early 20th century, with idols dated to the 7th century AD (all flagged as verify). The hill rises about 750 feet above the town; pilgrims climb roughly 200 steps (a 1.5 km strenuous trek) or use the ropeway.

name: Savitri Temple
town_description: Pushkar is a small holy town in Ajmer district, Rajasthan, built around the sacred Pushkar Lake and ringed by hills on three sides - Ratnagiri to the south, Nilgiri to the north, Sanchoora to the west and Suryagiri to the east. The Savitri Temple crowns Ratnagiri, the highest of these hills.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport is the nearest airport (~150 km).
travel.railway: Ajmer Railway Station is the nearest railhead (~17 km).
travel.road: 2 km east of Pushkar town on Kharekhari Road; a ropeway (Rs 100 both ways, 7:30 AM-8:00 PM) or a ~200-step climb reaches the hilltop shrine.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; sunrise and sunset views from the hilltop are the highlight.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM (per MakeMyTrip). Shoes not allowed inside; wear comfortable footwear for the climb and carry water.
